notes: Putting new lockers in stores goes against the key (apartment buildings): wrong-recommendation flag (rule 9). It ignores that store lockers are only 30% full (rule 7). Every number it states matches the sheet, so it passes consistency (rule 4 judges stated numbers, not the recommendation).

responses.value: Expand to 5,000 lockers, mostly in stores, where shoppers already go. Each $8,000 locker earns $2,500 a year at 80% full, a 3-year payback, and building owners have offered 2,500 sites. The risk is slow fill, so start with 500 new store lockers.
